newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar to seek retest of highs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar to seek retest of highs.

text.p: The dollar's ability to quickly bounce back from dips indicated it may retest its recent highs soon, analysts said on Thursday.

Dollar/mark is about one pfennig away from 1.8490, its highest level since November 1989, made on Monday. Dollar/yen is within reach of key resistance at 119.00, the 50-percent retracement of the 126.47-110.62 move, the 1997 high-low.
Dollar/Swiss is about 1-1/2 centime away from the retest of the 47-month high at 1.5261, set on Wednesday.
"There is an important resistance above 1.85 marks," said Dan Ascani, president of Global Market Strategists.

Analysts said the potential for fresh dollar/mark gains is preserved for as long as 1.8250-support holds. It is the 38-percent retracement of the move from 1.7860, the July 17 low, to 1.8490, the high on Monday.

The dollar/yen upside should remain in place unless 117.90, the 50-percent retracement of the 116.85/118.95 move this week, gives way. That level was breached overnight -- but not convincingly -- when the dollar dipped to 117.48 yen.
"The dollar has gotten into the habit of pausing before the U.S. economic numbers come out, and then to take off again," Ascani noted.
The dollar slipped ahead of the second-quarter U.S. Gross Domestic Product on Thursday and consolidated ahead of the July jobs data due out on Friday at 1230 GMT.

"The dollar may do much like last night, wait for the payrolls like it waited for the GDP, and take off again," said Ascani who expected dollar/mark to soon climb to 1.86, based on projections off the rally's base in the 1.77/80 area.

Ascani also described 119 yen as a fairly important level with 121 yen the objective for the rally started in June, off the 1997 low. The 121-yen level is also the 62-percent retracement of the high/low move.
Scott Siller, senior analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch, expected the dollar/mark rally to reach 1.8675, based on trendlines from the lows of November and May.
The dollar/mark gains may be slowed down by an extension of the mark/yen's recovery above 64.65
"It would take a move below 63.50 yen to resume the medium-term bear trend in mark/yen," Siller said.
Sterling/mark continued its correction from recent lows at 2.9725 but needs to climb back above 3.03, the 50-percent retracement of the latest slide, to signal a new rally.
